learning_outcomes.text: Have profound knowledge of the statistical and mathematical tools utilized in the different phases of the process development
Have knowledge and understanding of the industrial context where to apply this know-how
Understand and explain the chemical and biological phenomena under study by using these statistical tools
Understand how carry out a process study taking in consideration industrial cases that will be discussed in the ambit of this course
Demonstrate skill ability to analyze different industrial cases applying the statistical tools discussed in this module
Have reasoning ability in the development of an industrial process and the ability to face it by applying the course knowledge in an integrated and comprehensive manner
Demonstrate the capacity for reading and understand some tools of multivariate analysis (tools not included in this course)

syllabus_topics: Steps utilized in the process development and its optimization: lab-scale tests, pilot plant tests, industrial application of the developed processes. Scale-up and Scale-down.
Main statistical parameters: average, variance, standard deviation, covariance, range
Histogram and main distribution of probabilities
Statistical tests, power of the test, control charts, Cp and Cpk
Linear and non-linear regression. Parameter estimation of mathematical models (algebraic and differential models)
Factorial experiments with more factors and levels. Data analysis
Fractional factorial experiments, evaluation of aliases
Response Surface Methodology (RSM) in the optimization of chemical and biotechnological processes
assessment_rules: Summative assessment consists of a written test followed by an oral examination. An optional mid-term written test can be taken to split the workload; if passed, the student takes a final oral test. The written test involves 2-3 exercises with multiple questions, to be solved within 3 hours. The oral examination typically lasts less than 1 hour and covers areas needing clarification from the written test and additional subjects from the course program.
bibliography: Montgomery D.C. Design and Analysis of Experiments. JW&S
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Industriale (Industrial Engineering), classe L-9 Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria industriale
